beats.summary: Deangelo announces big changes and sets a strict tone for the office.

evidence.snippet: So, coasting time is officially over. Big changes are comin', and they're comin' fast.
I like my life outside of this place. I live to leave at 5.

beats.summary: Deangelo expresses distrust about people telling him what he wants to hear and wants to identify genuine workers.

evidence.snippet: Once they figure me out, they start to tell me what I want to hear.
I need to quickly figure out who's a good worker and who is simply a good mind reader.

beats.summary: Deangelo gives Toby a new chair and enforces a take-it-or-leave-it attitude about changes.

evidence.snippet: Change two, Toby, you're gettin' a new chair.
I don't care what your favorite flavor is. Here's a bowl of ice cream. You either like it or you don't.

beats.summary: Deangelo tries to build rapport with Dwight but Dwight remains distant and uninterested.

evidence.snippet: Listen. I've got a sixer. "Automatic for the People" on the jukebox. Let's hit the park after sundown.
No matter how many times I reach out to Dwight, he doesn't seem to want anything to do with me.

beats.summary: Deangelo and Dwight engage in a back-and-forth about liking each other, with Dwight resisting Deangelo's attempts.

evidence.snippet: You know what… straight up, why don't you like me?
I'm just not a suck-up like everyone else around here.

beats.summary: There is talk about an 'inner circle' in the office, with some characters denying its existence and others claiming membership.

evidence.snippet: There is no inner circle. Deangelo just prefers to delegate a few things, to a few guys.
Kevin Malone, is IN the inner circle! Which doesn't exist.
